blocks.es_reference: 📖 Cristianismo Radical: Los Diez Mandamientos de Jesús — Unidad 12: Sed Hacedores de Discípulos

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations... teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you." — Matthew 28:19-20 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones... enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado." — Mateo 28:19-20 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. The Church's Marching Orders
blocks.es_reference: 1. Las Órdenes de Marcha de la Iglesia

blocks.en: Matthew 28:19-20 (NKJV): "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age."
blocks.es_reference: Mateo 28:19-20 (RVG): "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándolos en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo; enseñándoles que guarden todas las cosas que os he mandado; y he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo."

blocks.en: These are the last words of Jesus before He ascended, and last words carry weight. He did not leave His church a vague encouragement to be religious; He left a commission, a marching order: go and make disciples. Everything else the church does — its worship, its teaching, its gathering — finds its purpose in this. The risen Lord, to whom all authority in heaven and earth has been given, sends His people out to reproduce His followers in every nation, and promises His own presence to the very end.
blocks.es_reference: Éstas son las últimas palabras de Jesús antes de ascender, y las últimas palabras tienen peso. No dejó a su iglesia un aliento vago a ser religiosa; dejó una comisión, una orden de marcha: id y haced discípulos. Todo lo demás que la iglesia hace — su adoración, su enseñanza, su reunión — halla su propósito en esto. El Señor resucitado, a quien se le ha dado toda autoridad en el cielo y en la tierra, envía a su pueblo a reproducir a sus seguidores en cada nación, y promete su propia presencia hasta el fin mismo.

blocks.en: Notice carefully what He commands. Not "make converts," not "make crowds," not "make church members," but "make disciples" — disciples taught "to observe all things" He commanded. The goal is not a decision and a handshake; it is a life remade in obedience to Christ. To be a disciple-maker is to take seriously that the whole point of the Christian life is to follow Jesus and to help others follow Him too. This unit is about answering that commission.
blocks.es_reference: Note con cuidado lo que manda. No "haced conversos," ni "haced multitudes," ni "haced miembros de iglesia," sino "haced discípulos" — discípulos enseñados a "guardar todas las cosas" que mandó. La meta no es una decisión y un apretón de manos; es una vida rehecha en obediencia a Cristo. Ser hacedor de discípulos es tomar en serio que todo el sentido de la vida cristiana es seguir a Jesús y ayudar a otros a seguirlo también. Esta unidad se trata de responder a esa comisión.

blocks.en: 2. All Believers Are Disciples
blocks.es_reference: 2. Todos los Creyentes Son Discípulos

blocks.en: We must clear away a common misunderstanding before we go further. Many people imagine that "disciple" is an advanced category — that there are ordinary Christians and then there are a special few "disciples." But the New Testament will not allow this. Before the followers of Jesus were ever called "Christians," they were called "disciples," and not just the Twelve — all believers in Jesus are called disciples in the New Testament. The word simply means "one who learns," one who follows a teacher to become like Him.
blocks.es_reference: Debemos despejar un malentendido común antes de seguir. Muchos imaginan que "discípulo" es una categoría avanzada — que hay cristianos comunes y luego unos pocos especiales que son "discípulos." Pero el Nuevo Testamento no lo permite. Antes de que los seguidores de Jesús fueran llamados "cristianos," fueron llamados "discípulos," y no solo los doce — todos los creyentes en Jesús son llamados discípulos en el Nuevo Testamento. La palabra sencillamente significa "uno que aprende," uno que sigue a un maestro para llegar a ser como Él.

blocks.en: This means that radical discipleship is not an elite track; it is normal Christianity. There are not two forms of the faith, a casual version and a committed version. It is impossible to be saved and yet not be in a living relationship with Jesus, following Him; those who teach a cheap grace that promises salvation without repentance and discipleship are leading people astray. Jesus said you cannot pour new wine into old wineskins, and genuine discipleship will never develop inside the brittle old skins of mere tradition and religiosity — what we might call "churchianity." The new wine of following Jesus requires a new wineskin: a life actually surrendered to Him.
blocks.es_reference: Esto significa que el discipulado radical no es una vía de élite; es el cristianismo normal. No hay dos formas de la fe, una versión casual y una versión comprometida. Es imposible ser salvo y a la vez no estar en una relación viva con Jesús, siguiéndolo; quienes enseñan una gracia barata que promete salvación sin arrepentimiento ni discipulado están extraviando a la gente. Jesús dijo que no se puede echar vino nuevo en odres viejos, y el discipulado genuino nunca se desarrollará dentro de los frágiles odres viejos de la mera tradición y religiosidad — lo que podríamos llamar "religionismo." El vino nuevo de seguir a Jesús requiere un odre nuevo: una vida de veras rendida a Él.

blocks.en: 3. Disciples Cannot Be Mass-Produced
blocks.es_reference: 3. Los Discípulos No Se Producen en Masa

blocks.en: If the goal is disciples and not merely crowds, then the method matters enormously — because disciples cannot be mass-produced. There is certainly a place for large gatherings; Jesus Himself taught the multitudes. But notice where He invested His life: in twelve men, and sometimes only three of those twelve. He preached to thousands, but He poured Himself into a few. That is not an accident of His ministry; it is the pattern of how disciples are actually made.
blocks.es_reference: Si la meta son discípulos y no meras multitudes, entonces el método importa enormemente — porque los discípulos no se producen en masa. Ciertamente hay lugar para las grandes reuniones; Jesús mismo enseñó a las multitudes. Pero note dónde invirtió su vida: en doce hombres, y a veces solo en tres de esos doce. Predicó a miles, pero se derramó en unos pocos. Eso no es un accidente de su ministerio; es el patrón de cómo se hacen en realidad los discípulos.

blocks.en: Making disciples the way Jesus did means spending large amounts of time with small numbers of people. You cannot disciple a stadium. Real formation happens up close, life on life, where someone can see how a more mature believer prays, handles trouble, loves a spouse, forgives an enemy, and walks with God day by day. This is why small groups are such a proven and biblically sound method: as the numbers get smaller, the odds of genuine discipleship go up. The disciple-maker is willing to think small on purpose, investing deeply in a few rather than shallowly in many.
blocks.es_reference: Hacer discípulos a la manera de Jesús significa pasar grandes cantidades de tiempo con números pequeños de personas. No se puede discipular un estadio. La formación real sucede de cerca, vida con vida, donde alguien puede ver cómo un creyente más maduro ora, maneja la dificultad, ama a su cónyuge, perdona a un enemigo, y camina con Dios día tras día. Por esto los grupos pequeños son un método tan probado y bíblicamente sólido: a medida que los números se hacen más pequeños, las probabilidades del discipulado genuino suben. El hacedor de discípulos está dispuesto a pensar en pequeño a propósito, invirtiendo hondamente en unos pocos en vez de superficialmente en muchos.

blocks.en: 4. Every Christian a Minister
blocks.es_reference: 4. Cada Cristiano un Ministro

blocks.en: Ephesians 4:11-12 (NKJV): "And He Himself gave some to be apostles... and some pastors and teachers, for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ."
blocks.es_reference: Efesios 4:11-12 (RVG): "Y él mismo dio unos, apóstoles... y otros, pastores y maestros; a fin de perfeccionar a los santos para la obra del ministerio, para la edificación del cuerpo de Cristo."

blocks.en: Here is one of the most freeing truths in the New Testament, and it is essential to disciple-making. The goal of all Christian teaching is to produce ministers. Ephesians gives church leadership essentially one job: to equip the saints — that is, ordinary believers — to do the work of ministry. God's goal for every Christian's life is that they contribute, that their efforts make a real difference for the kingdom.
blocks.es_reference: He aquí una de las verdades más liberadoras del Nuevo Testamento, y es esencial para hacer discípulos. La meta de toda enseñanza cristiana es producir ministros. Efesios da al liderazgo de la iglesia esencialmente un solo trabajo: perfeccionar a los santos — es decir, a los creyentes comunes — para hacer la obra del ministerio. La meta de Dios para la vida de cada cristiano es que contribuya, que sus esfuerzos hagan una diferencia real para el reino.

blocks.en: This overturns the common picture in which a few professionals do the ministry while everyone else watches. The purpose of God-appointed leaders is not to do the ministry themselves, but to equip the saints to do it. A pastor's real job is to make ordinary believers effective as ministers. All Christians are ministers, priests, and witnesses; leaders exist to train and release them. A disciple-maker, therefore, is not trying to create an audience dependent on him, but to raise up other ministers — people who will in turn serve and disciple still others. The measure of success is not how many come to watch, but how many are sent out to work.
blocks.es_reference: Esto trastorna el cuadro común en el que unos pocos profesionales hacen el ministerio mientras los demás observan. El propósito de los líderes designados por Dios no es hacer el ministerio ellos mismos, sino perfeccionar a los santos para que lo hagan. El verdadero trabajo de un pastor es hacer eficaces a los creyentes comunes como ministros. Todos los cristianos son ministros, sacerdotes, y testigos; los líderes existen para entrenarlos y soltarlos. Un hacedor de discípulos, por tanto, no trata de crear una audiencia dependiente de él, sino de levantar a otros ministros — personas que a su vez servirán y discipularán a otros más. La medida del éxito no es cuántos vienen a observar, sino cuántos son enviados a trabajar.

blocks.en: 5. The Disciple-Maker Takes Up a Towel
blocks.es_reference: 5. El Hacedor de Discípulos Toma una Toalla

blocks.en: John 13:14-15 (NKJV): "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you."
blocks.es_reference: Juan 13:14-15 (RVG): "Pues si yo, el Señor y el Maestro, he lavado vuestros pies, vosotros también debéis lavaros los pies los unos a los otros. Porque ejemplo os he dado, para que como yo os he hecho, vosotros también hagáis."

blocks.en: But how does a disciple-maker lead? Not from a throne, but with a towel. On the night He was betrayed, knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, Jesus rose from supper, wrapped a towel around His waist, and washed His disciples' feet. In the upper room everyone saw the dirty feet, but only Jesus saw an opportunity to serve. He took up a towel, not a title. That is the posture of every true disciple-maker: leading by serving, seeing the needs that others overlook, and stooping to meet them.
blocks.es_reference: Pero ¿cómo lidera un hacedor de discípulos? No desde un trono, sino con una toalla. La noche en que fue entregado, sabiendo que el Padre había puesto todas las cosas en sus manos, Jesús se levantó de la cena, se ciñó una toalla a la cintura, y lavó los pies de sus discípulos. En el aposento alto todos vieron los pies sucios, pero solo Jesús vio una oportunidad de servir. Tomó una toalla, no un título. Ésa es la postura de todo verdadero hacedor de discípulos: liderar sirviendo, ver las necesidades que otros pasan por alto, y abajarse para suplirlas.

blocks.en: The missionary's towel: A veteran missionary, asked near the end of four decades of labor to sum up his life's work, did not list his accomplishments or count his converts. He said simply, "Just say I tried to wash feet." After forty years of service, that was the legacy he wanted: not a monument, not a title, just a towel. The disciple-maker who has truly caught the heart of Jesus measures a life not by what he achieved, but by whom he served.
blocks.es_reference: La toalla del misionero: A un misionero veterano, al pedírsele cerca del final de cuatro décadas de labor que resumiera la obra de su vida, no enumeró sus logros ni contó sus convertidos. Dijo sencillamente: "Solo digan que traté de lavar pies." Tras cuarenta años de servicio, ése era el legado que quería: no un monumento, no un título, solo una toalla. El hacedor de discípulos que de veras ha captado el corazón de Jesús mide una vida no por lo que logró, sino por a quién sirvió.

blocks.en: This is the great correction to every worldly idea of leadership. We are tempted to think that to lead and shape others is to rise above them; Jesus shows that it is to kneel before them. The one who would make disciples must first be a servant, because he is reproducing not his own importance but the character of the Servant-King. You cannot disciple people into Christlikeness from a posture Christ never took.
blocks.es_reference: Ésta es la gran corrección a toda idea mundana del liderazgo. Nos tienta pensar que liderar y formar a otros es elevarse por encima de ellos; Jesús muestra que es arrodillarse ante ellos. El que quiera hacer discípulos debe ser primero un siervo, porque está reproduciendo no su propia importancia sino el carácter del Rey-Siervo. No se puede discipular a las personas a la semejanza de Cristo desde una postura que Cristo nunca tomó.

blocks.en: 6. Serving Even the Undeserving
blocks.es_reference: 6. Servir Aun a los Inmerecedores

blocks.en: The towel reaches further than we would like. On that same night, Jesus washed the feet of every disciple in the room — including Judas, the man He knew would betray Him within hours. The Lord knelt before His betrayer and washed his feet. Love served even the undeserving. This tells us that the disciple-maker's service is not reserved for the promising, the grateful, or the deserving; it is poured out even on those who will disappoint us.
blocks.es_reference: La toalla alcanza más lejos de lo que quisiéramos. Esa misma noche, Jesús lavó los pies de cada discípulo en el aposento — incluido Judas, el hombre que sabía que lo traicionaría en pocas horas. El Señor se arrodilló ante su traidor y le lavó los pies. El amor sirvió aun al inmerecedor. Esto nos dice que el servicio del hacedor de discípulos no se reserva para los prometedores, los agradecidos, o los que lo merecen; se derrama aun sobre quienes nos decepcionarán.

blocks.en: "Our way of washing feet": An elderly couple quietly ran a small soup ministry, feeding people year after year with no fanfare and no expectation of return. When someone asked them why they kept at it, they answered simply, "It's our way of washing feet." They had grasped what Jesus meant: that the humble, unglamorous service of those who can never repay you is exactly where the towel of Christ is taken up today.
blocks.es_reference: "Nuestra manera de lavar pies": Una pareja anciana llevaba calladamente un pequeño ministerio de sopa, alimentando a la gente año tras año sin fanfarria y sin expectativa de retorno. Cuando alguien les preguntó por qué seguían en ello, respondieron sencillamente: "Es nuestra manera de lavar pies." Habían captado lo que Jesús quiso decir: que el servicio humilde y poco glamoroso a quienes nunca pueden recompensarte es exactamente donde se toma hoy la toalla de Cristo.

blocks.en: Jesus taught this directly: when you give a feast, invite those who cannot repay you, and you will be blessed, because they have nothing to give back. That is precisely how God served us, for we could never repay Him. So we serve not to be thanked and not to earn a reward, but out of gratitude for having been served by Christ. As Jesus said, when we have done everything we were told, we should still say, "we are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty." We serve from redemption, not for recognition.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús lo enseñó directamente: cuando hagas un banquete, invita a los que no pueden recompensarte, y serás bendecido, porque nada tienen que devolver. Así es exactamente como Dios nos sirvió, pues nunca podríamos recompensarle. Así que servimos no para ser agradecidos y no para ganar una recompensa, sino por gratitud de haber sido servidos por Cristo. Como dijo Jesús, cuando hayamos hecho todo lo que se nos mandó, todavía debemos decir: "siervos inútiles somos; lo que debíamos hacer, hicimos." Servimos desde la redención, no por reconocimiento.

blocks.en: 7. Multiplication: Faithful to Faithful
blocks.es_reference: 7. Multiplicación: de Fiel a Fiel

blocks.en: 2 Timothy 2:2 (NKJV): "And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also."
blocks.es_reference: 2 Timoteo 2:2 (RVG): "Y lo que has oído de mí entre muchos testigos, esto encarga a hombres fieles que sean idóneos para enseñar también a otros."

blocks.en: Disciple-making has a forward momentum built into it: it is meant to multiply. Paul tells Timothy to take what he has received and commit it to faithful people who will be able to teach others also. Count the generations in that single verse: Paul, to Timothy, to faithful people, to others also — four links in a chain that is designed never to stop. A disciple-maker does not merely gather followers; he raises up people who will themselves make disciples, who will in turn raise up still others.
blocks.es_reference: El hacer discípulos tiene un impulso hacia adelante incorporado: está hecho para multiplicarse. Pablo le dice a Timoteo que tome lo que ha recibido y lo encargue a personas fieles que sean idóneas para enseñar también a otros. Cuente las generaciones en ese solo versículo: Pablo, a Timoteo, a personas fieles, a otros también — cuatro eslabones en una cadena diseñada para nunca detenerse. Un hacedor de discípulos no solo reúne seguidores; levanta a personas que ellas mismas harán discípulos, que a su vez levantarán a otros más.

blocks.en: This is how the gospel was always meant to spread — through lives reproducing lives, whether that happens in a home, a small group, or a church with a full program calendar. The early church multiplied this way too: when a group meeting in a home grew too large, they simply began to meet in two homes — one simple, faithful way to expand, though certainly not the only one. Multiplication is the natural fruit of real discipleship: a disciple who has truly been formed will, sooner or later, begin forming others.
blocks.es_reference: Así es como el evangelio siempre estuvo destinado a esparcirse — a través de vidas que reproducen vidas, ya sea que esto suceda en una casa, un grupo pequeño, o una iglesia con un calendario completo de programas. La iglesia primitiva también se multiplicó así: cuando un grupo que se reunía en una casa se hacía demasiado grande, sencillamente empezaban a reunirse en dos casas — una manera simple y fiel de expandirse, aunque ciertamente no la única. La multiplicación es el fruto natural del discipulado real: un discípulo que de veras ha sido formado, tarde o temprano, empezará a formar a otros.

blocks.en: 8. From a "Bless-Me Club" to an Army
blocks.es_reference: 8. De un "Club Bendíceme" a un Ejército

blocks.en: All of this calls for a fundamental change in how we think about the church. It is easy to slip into treating the church as a "bless-me club" — a place concerned mainly with meeting our own needs and ensuring its own comfortable survival. Too often the church has taken a defensive posture, functioning like a hospital that exists only to care for the wants of those already inside, while the great needs of the world and the unfinished Great Commission go unaddressed. But that is not why Jesus left us here.
blocks.es_reference: Todo esto exige un cambio fundamental en cómo pensamos en la iglesia. Es fácil caer en tratar a la iglesia como un "club bendíceme" — un lugar preocupado principalmente por suplir nuestras propias necesidades y asegurar su propia supervivencia cómoda. Con demasiada frecuencia la iglesia ha tomado una postura defensiva, funcionando como un hospital que existe solo para cuidar los deseos de los que ya están adentro, mientras las grandes necesidades del mundo y la Gran Comisión inconclusa quedan sin atender. Pero no es por eso que Jesús nos dejó aquí.

blocks.en: It is time to take the offensive — to stop being a fortress and start being an army, going out to evangelize the world and to make disciples of all nations. A fresh breeze is blowing, calling the church back to the humility, simplicity, and mutuality of the New Testament believers, and toward the final fulfillment of the Great Commission. God is not looking for spectators; He is looking for soldiers — ordinary disciples who will give themselves to the mission of making other disciples. The question for each of us is whether we will remain consumers of religious services or become reproducers of the life of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Es tiempo de tomar la ofensiva — de dejar de ser una fortaleza y empezar a ser un ejército, saliendo a evangelizar el mundo y a hacer discípulos de todas las naciones. Una brisa fresca está soplando, llamando a la iglesia de vuelta a la humildad, la sencillez, y la mutualidad de los creyentes del Nuevo Testamento, y hacia el cumplimiento final de la Gran Comisión. Dios no busca espectadores; busca soldados — discípulos comunes que se entreguen a la misión de hacer otros discípulos. La pregunta para cada uno de nosotros es si seguiremos siendo consumidores de servicios religiosos o nos volveremos reproductores de la vida de Cristo.

blocks.en: 9. Whose Feet Can I Wash Today?
blocks.es_reference: 9. ¿A Quién Puedo Lavar los Pies Hoy?

blocks.en: So the great commission comes down, in the end, to something surprisingly humble and daily. The disciple-maker holds two things together: the towel and the mission. He serves the few God has placed near him — washing their feet, bearing with their faults as Christ bore with Judas, investing his life in them up close — and in doing so he reproduces in them the very life of Jesus, who then reproduce it in others, and so the kingdom advances. It is not glamorous work. The world crowns achievers; heaven crowns servants.
blocks.es_reference: Así que la gran comisión se reduce, al final, a algo sorprendentemente humilde y diario. El hacedor de discípulos sostiene juntas dos cosas: la toalla y la misión. Sirve a los pocos que Dios ha puesto cerca de él — lavándoles los pies, soportando sus faltas como Cristo soportó a Judas, invirtiendo su vida en ellos de cerca — y al hacerlo reproduce en ellos la vida misma de Jesús, quienes luego la reproducen en otros, y así avanza el reino. No es trabajo glamoroso. El mundo corona a los triunfadores; el cielo corona a los siervos.

blocks.en: A good way to begin is with a simple daily question: "Lord, whose feet can I wash today?" Take one towel moment this week — serve someone who cannot repay you, invest in someone younger in the faith, share Christ with someone who does not yet know Him. The Lord who gave the commission also gave the promise that seals it: "lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age." We do not make disciples in our own strength or alone. We go in His company and His power. And He said it plainly: "if you know these things, blessed are you if you do them."
blocks.es_reference: Una buena manera de empezar es con una simple pregunta diaria: "Señor, ¿a quién puedo lavar los pies hoy?" Toma un momento de toalla esta semana — sirve a alguien que no puede recompensarte, invierte en alguien más joven en la fe, comparte a Cristo con alguien que aún no lo conoce. El Señor que dio la comisión también dio la promesa que la sella: "he aquí, yo estoy con vosotros todos los días, hasta el fin del mundo." No hacemos discípulos por nuestra propia fuerza ni solos. Vamos en su compañía y su poder. Y lo dijo con claridad: "si sabéis estas cosas, bienaventurados seréis si las hiciereis."

mc.stem: In Matthew 28:19-20, what does Jesus command His church to make?
options: Disciples — taught to observe all He commanded
mc.why: Jesus commands 'make disciples,' not converts or crowds — disciples taught to observe all He commanded; the goal is a life remade in obedience, not a decision and a handshake.

mc.stem: What promise seals the Great Commission?
options: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age'
mc.why: The risen Lord, given all authority, promises His own presence to the very end — we do not make disciples in our own strength but in His company and power.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what does the New Testament call ALL believers?
options: All believers are called 'disciples' — the word means 'one who learns'
mc.why: Before they were called 'Christians' they were called 'disciples,' and not just the Twelve — all believers are disciples; the word means 'one who learns.'

mc.stem: How does the lesson describe 'churchianity' versus discipleship?
options: Discipleship won't develop in the old wineskins of mere tradition and religiosity
mc.why: Genuine discipleship will never develop inside the brittle old wineskins of mere tradition and religiosity ('churchianity'); the new wine needs a life surrendered to Jesus.

mc.stem: Why does the lesson say 'disciples cannot be mass-produced'?
options: Jesus taught the masses but invested His life in twelve, sometimes only three — life on life
mc.why: Jesus taught multitudes but poured Himself into twelve, sometimes three; real formation happens up close, life on life — you cannot disciple a stadium.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, why are small groups a sound method for discipleship?
options: As numbers get smaller, the odds of genuine discipleship go up
mc.why: Making disciples means spending large amounts of time with small numbers; as the numbers get smaller, the odds of genuine discipleship go up — invest deeply in a few.

mc.stem: According to Ephesians 4:11-12, what is the one job of church leadership?
options: To do all the ministry themselves
To equip the saints to do the work of ministry
mc.why: Ephesians gives leadership one job: to equip the saints — ordinary believers — to do the work of ministry; a pastor's job is to make believers effective as ministers.

mc.stem: What does the lesson say is the measure of a disciple-maker's success?
options: How many are sent out to work as ministers themselves
mc.why: A disciple-maker raises up other ministers, not a dependent audience; the measure of success is not how many come to watch but how many are sent out to work.

options: With a towel — leading by serving, taking up a towel, not a title
mc.why: Jesus wrapped a towel and washed feet; in the upper room only He saw an opportunity to serve. He took up a towel, not a title — the posture of every disciple-maker.

mc.stem: What did the veteran missionary say summed up his life's work?
options: 'Just say I tried to wash feet'
mc.why: After forty years, the missionary did not list accomplishments; he said, 'Just say I tried to wash feet' — measuring life not by achievement but by whom he served.

mc.stem: Whose feet did Jesus wash, and what does it teach disciple-makers?
options: Even Judas's — service is not reserved for the deserving but poured out even on those who disappoint us
mc.why: Jesus washed even Judas's feet, knowing he would betray Him; love served the undeserving, so the disciple-maker's service is not reserved for the promising or grateful.

mc.why: The couple fed people year after year with no fanfare, calling it 'our way of washing feet' — the humble service of those who can never repay is where Christ's towel is taken up.

options: Four — Paul, to Timothy, to faithful people, to others also
mc.why: Paul to Timothy to faithful people to others also — four links in a chain designed never to stop; disciple-making is meant to multiply.

mc.why: When a home group grew too large, they simply began meeting in two homes — a simple way to expand with no costly buildings, freeing resources for the Commission and the poor.

mc.stem: What does the lesson mean by the church becoming a 'bless-me club'?
options: Concerned mainly with its own needs and survival rather than the world's needs and the Commission
mc.why: A 'bless-me club' is concerned mainly with its own needs and comfortable survival, taking a defensive posture like a hospital, while the world's needs and the Commission go unaddressed.

options: To take the offensive — to be an army going out to make disciples of all nations

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what two things does the disciple-maker hold together?
options: The towel and the mission — serving the few and reproducing Christ's life in them
mc.why: The disciple-maker holds together the towel and the mission: serving the few God places near him and reproducing the life of Jesus in them, who then reproduce it in others.

mc.stem: What daily question does the lesson suggest for the disciple-maker?

sa.prompt: Explain the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20) and what it commands the church to do.
sa.model: These are the last words of Jesus before He ascended, and last words carry weight. He did not leave His church a vague encouragement to be religious but a commission, a marching order: go and make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe all He commanded. Everything else the church does finds its purpose here. The risen Lord, to whom all authority in heaven and earth has been given, sends His people to reproduce His followers in every nation and promises His own presence to the very end. Notice what He commands: not make converts, crowds, or church members, but make disciples taught to observe all things He commanded. The goal is not a decision and a handshake but a life remade in obedience to Christ, so to be a disciple-maker is to take seriously that the whole point of the Christian life is to follow Jesus and help others follow Him too.

sa.prompt: Explain why all believers are disciples and how this makes discipleship 'normal Christianity.'
sa.model: We must clear away a common misunderstanding, for many imagine that disciple is an advanced category, that there are ordinary Christians and then a special few disciples. But the New Testament will not allow this, for before the followers of Jesus were called Christians they were called disciples, and not just the Twelve, since all believers are called disciples; the word means one who learns, one who follows a teacher to become like Him. This means radical discipleship is not an elite track but normal Christianity. There are not two forms of the faith, a casual and a committed version, for it is impossible to be saved and yet not be in a living relationship with Jesus, following Him, and those who teach a cheap grace promising salvation without repentance and discipleship lead people astray. Jesus said you cannot pour new wine into old wineskins, and genuine discipleship will never develop inside the brittle skins of tradition and religiosity.

sa.prompt: Explain why 'disciples cannot be mass-produced' and what method Jesus used.
sa.model: If the goal is disciples and not merely crowds, the method matters enormously, because disciples cannot be mass-produced. There is a place for large gatherings, and Jesus Himself taught the multitudes, but notice where He invested His life: in twelve men, and sometimes only three of those twelve. He preached to thousands but poured Himself into a few, and that is the pattern of how disciples are actually made. Making disciples the way Jesus did means spending large amounts of time with small numbers of people, for you cannot disciple a stadium. Real formation happens up close, life on life, where someone can see how a mature believer prays, handles trouble, forgives an enemy, and walks with God day by day. This is why small groups are a proven and biblically sound method: as the numbers get smaller, the odds of genuine discipleship go up, and the disciple-maker is willing to think small on purpose, investing deeply in a few rather than shallowly in many.

sa.prompt: Explain Ephesians 4:11-12 and how it overturns the idea that only professionals minister.
sa.model: Here is one of the most freeing truths in the New Testament, essential to disciple-making: the goal of all Christian teaching is to produce ministers. Ephesians gives church leadership essentially one job, to equip the saints, that is ordinary believers, to do the work of ministry, for God's goal for every Christian's life is that they contribute and that their efforts make a real difference for the kingdom. This overturns the common picture in which a few professionals do the ministry while everyone else watches. The purpose of God-appointed leaders is not to do the ministry themselves but to equip the saints to do it, so a pastor's real job is to make ordinary believers effective as ministers. All Christians are ministers, priests, and witnesses, and leaders exist to train and release them. A disciple-maker is therefore not trying to create a dependent audience but to raise up other ministers, and the measure of success is not how many come to watch but how many are sent out to work.

sa.prompt: Using John 13, explain how the disciple-maker leads, and the missionary's towel.
sa.model: How does a disciple-maker lead? Not from a throne but with a towel. On the night He was betrayed, knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, Jesus rose, wrapped a towel around His waist, and washed His disciples' feet. In the upper room everyone saw the dirty feet, but only Jesus saw an opportunity to serve; He took up a towel, not a title, and that is the posture of every true disciple-maker, leading by serving and stooping to meet the needs others overlook. A veteran missionary, asked near the end of forty years to sum up his life's work, did not list accomplishments or count converts but said simply, just say I tried to wash feet. That was the legacy he wanted, not a monument or a title but a towel. We are tempted to think that to lead and shape others is to rise above them, but Jesus shows it is to kneel before them, for you cannot disciple people into Christlikeness from a posture Christ never took.

sa.prompt: Explain how Jesus washing Judas's feet shapes the disciple-maker's service.
sa.model: The towel reaches further than we would like, for on that same night Jesus washed the feet of every disciple in the room, including Judas, the man He knew would betray Him within hours. The Lord knelt before His betrayer and washed his feet, so love served even the undeserving, which tells us the disciple-maker's service is not reserved for the promising, the grateful, or the deserving but is poured out even on those who will disappoint us. An elderly couple quietly ran a small soup ministry for years with no fanfare and no expectation of return, and when asked why, they answered, it's our way of washing feet. Jesus taught this directly, saying when you give a feast invite those who cannot repay you and you will be blessed, for that is how God served us, since we could never repay Him. So we serve not to be thanked or to earn a reward but out of gratitude, and even having done all, we say we are unworthy servants; we serve from redemption, not for recognition.

sa.prompt: Explain how 2 Timothy 2:2 and the early church show disciple-making multiplies.
sa.model: Disciple-making has a forward momentum built into it, for it is meant to multiply. Paul tells Timothy to take what he has received and commit it to faithful people who will be able to teach others also, and we can count the generations in that single verse: Paul, to Timothy, to faithful people, to others also, four links in a chain designed never to stop. A disciple-maker does not merely gather followers but raises up people who will themselves make disciples, who will in turn raise up still others. This is how the gospel was always meant to spread, through lives reproducing lives, whether in a home or a church with a full program. The early church multiplied this way too: when a group meeting in a home grew too large, they simply began to meet in two homes, one simple, faithful way to expand, though not the only one. Multiplication is the natural fruit of real discipleship, for a disciple who has truly been formed will sooner or later begin forming others.

sa.prompt: Explain the call to move from a 'bless-me club' to an army, with Krupp's 'fresh breeze.'
sa.model: All of this calls for a fundamental change in how we think about the church, for it is easy to slip into treating the church as a bless-me club, concerned mainly with meeting our own needs and ensuring its own comfortable survival. Too often the church has taken a defensive posture, functioning like a hospital that exists only to care for those already inside, while the great needs of the world and the unfinished Great Commission go unaddressed, but that is not why Jesus left us here. It is time to take the offensive, to stop being a fortress and start being an army, going out to evangelize the world and make disciples of all nations. A fresh breeze is blowing, calling the church back to the humility, simplicity, and mutuality of the New Testament believers and toward the final fulfillment of the Great Commission. God is not looking for spectators but soldiers, ordinary disciples who give themselves to the mission of making other disciples, and the question is whether we will remain consumers of religious services or become reproducers of the life of Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain how the disciple-maker holds the towel and the mission together day by day.
sa.model: The great commission comes down, in the end, to something surprisingly humble and daily, for the disciple-maker holds two things together, the towel and the mission. He serves the few God has placed near him, washing their feet, bearing with their faults as Christ bore with Judas, and investing his life in them up close, and in doing so he reproduces in them the very life of Jesus, who then reproduce it in others, so the kingdom advances. It is not glamorous work, for the world crowns achievers but heaven crowns servants. A good way to begin is the simple daily question, Lord, whose feet can I wash today, taking one towel moment this week to serve someone who cannot repay you, to invest in someone younger in the faith, or to share Christ with someone who does not yet know Him. We do not make disciples in our own strength or alone but in His company and power, for He promised, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.

sa.prompt: Summarize what it means to 'be a disciple-maker,' gathering the unit's threads.
sa.model: To be a disciple-maker is to answer the last command of Jesus, to go and make disciples of all nations, taught to obey all He commanded. It means recognizing that all believers are disciples and that discipleship is normal Christianity, not an elite track. Because disciples cannot be mass-produced, the disciple-maker invests deeply in a few, life on life, and aims not to create a dependent audience but to equip the saints so that every Christian becomes a minister. He leads with a towel, not a title, serving even the undeserving as Christ washed Judas's feet, and serving from redemption rather than for reward. His work is meant to multiply, faithful to faithful, lives reproducing lives until the church stops being a bless-me club and becomes an army on the offensive. So he holds the towel and the mission together, asking daily whose feet he can wash, knowing the blessing is not in merely knowing these things but, as Jesus said, in doing them.
